items.a: It's a good idea, especially on Fridays and Saturdays: the dining room is small. Book online or call +33 3 22 45 17 69.
Saraba is open in the evening, Tuesday to Saturday, from 7 pm to midnight. Closed on Sundays and Mondays.
Yes: mafé, yassa and beef curry are €12 to take away. Call us to order. Fish is served in the restaurant only. And if you can't finish your plate, we'll give you a doggy bag.

africain.metaTitle: African restaurant in Amiens, Saint-Leu quarter | Saraba
africain.metaDescription: Looking for African food in Amiens? Saraba, on rue des Majots in Saint-Leu, serves mafé, yassa and grilled fish Tuesday to Saturday evenings. Book online.
africain.title: An African restaurant in the heart of Saint-Leu
africain.lead: At 13 rue des Majots, Saraba cooks the great dishes of West Africa every evening, with a soft spot for Senegal.

sections.p: Beef mafé in peanut sauce, chicken yassa with lemon and onions, thiou with okra, beef curry: dishes that take their time, served generously. To start, accras, alokos and pastels are made for sharing.
The dining room is small and warm: bamboo walls, carved masks, a handwritten chalkboard. People come with friends, family or as a couple, and many leave wanting to come back, or with a doggy bag.
Saraba is open from 7 pm to midnight, Tuesday to Saturday. At weekends it's best to book: online in two minutes or on +33 3 22 45 17 69.

mafe.metaTitle: Mafé in Amiens: Saraba's beef mafé, rue des Majots
mafe.metaDescription: Where to eat great mafé in Amiens? At Saraba, beef mafé in peanut sauce is the house speciality: €14 to eat in, €12 to take away.
mafe.title: Saraba's mafé
mafe.lead: It's the dish reviewers mention most: beef mafé slow-cooked in a peanut sauce, served generously.

sections.p: Mafé is a West African dish, very popular in Senegal and Mali: meat slowly simmered in a sauce of peanut paste and tomato. At Saraba it also comes as okra mafé.
Beef mafé is €14 in the restaurant and €12 to take away. To take it home, call us on +33 3 22 45 17 69 and it will be ready when you arrive.
Start with accras or alokos and finish with a chocolate fondant. Next time, try the chicken yassa or the thiou with okra.
